rows.explanation: Fund a comprehensive study of environmental health hazards, including air quality and asthma, to learn the cumulative effects on cb #1. The study should include the DEP wastewater treatment plant. Community Board No. 1 has been impacted by many adverse environmental factors, including but not limited to air and traffic pollution, particulate matter, construction pollution (thousands of apartment building units constructed and under construction), widespread chemical contamination (three superfund sites, dozens of brownfield sites and one large-scale underground oil spill), and widespread lead-contaminated soil. A comprehensive study is needed to assess these impacts and develop resolutions, such as anti-asthma initiatives, to be implemented. The Study should include the DEP Newtown Creek Resource Recovery Facility

rows.agency_label: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: BKCB2 recommends increased DOHMH funding in BKCD2 for street-level air quality monitors through the NYC Community Air Survey (NYCCAS) program, and exploration of collaboration opportunities with our State DEC partners to implement rooftop monitors on our NYCHA campuses and the Manhattan and Brooklyn Bridges. Particulate matter that is 2.5m or smaller (""PM2.5"") penetrates deep into the lungs and bloodstream, causing chronic and often lethal heart and lung disease. Internal Combustion Engines (ICE) such as gas-powered vehicles are the leading source of PM2.5. Long term exposure to PM2.5 contributes to 1 out of 25 deaths in NYC, and per the 2018 Community Health Profile, the levels of fine particulate matter and the rate of child asthma emergency room visits are notably higher in BKCD2 than in NYC as a whole. BKCD2 contains 1.5 miles (12%) of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE) within its boundaries and has 3 Neighborhood Tabulation Areas in Brooklyn's 10 highest PM2.5 levels--the most of any Brooklyn Community District. This request is particularly urgent given the Trump Administration's recent reversal of the Biden Administration's EPA limits on PM2.5.
